title: Quasi-excellence lifts across an ideal of definition in characteristic zero
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian $\mathbf Q$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and let $J\subseteq A$ be an ideal. Assume that $A$ is $J$-adically complete [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring], meaning that the canonical map $A\longrightarrow\varprojlim_{n\geq1}A/J^n$ is an isomorphism. Then $A$ is quasi-excellent if and only if $A/J$ is quasi-excellent [def-exc-excellent-ring].

source.place: Exposé I, Théorème 9.2 (Gabber), printed p.17: a Noetherian I-adically complete ring with A/I quasi-excellent is quasi-excellent (no characteristic hypothesis); the converse holds since A/J is a finite type A-algebra. Characteristic-zero form: Temkin, arXiv:0904.1592v2, Theorem 2.1.6 and Remark 2.1.7 (Nishimura-Nishimura, Theorem B), printed p.9.

proof.text: First assume $A$ is quasi-excellent. The quotient map $A\to A/J$ is a finite type map (the empty list generates the algebra). By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-g-ring] its target is a G-ring. To check J-2 directly, any finite list generating an $(A/J)$-algebra also generates it as an $A$-algebra: each coefficient in $A/J$ has a lift in $A$. Its regular locus is therefore open by J-2 for $A$. This proves that $A/J$ is quasi-excellent by [def-exc-excellent-ring].

source.place: Tag 07PV, proposition-finite-type-over-G-ring; Tag 07QT, definition-excellent; Tag 07P7, definition-J

proof.text: Now assume $A/J$ is quasi-excellent. Suppose for contradiction that $A$ is not. Apply [lem-per-qe-normal-counterexample-reduction] to the actual Noetherian complete pair $(A,J)$, keeping its rational algebra structure. Obtain $R,x$ with all the listed properties: $0\ne x$ is a nonunit, $R$ is a normal Nagata universally catenary domain, all its nonzero quotients are quasi-excellent, but $R$ is not. In particular the auxiliary integral closures in finite extensions satisfy every hypothesis of the next two lemmas. The reduction includes passage to principal ideals and a maximal bad quotient; it does not assert the desired lifting theorem.

source.place: Kurano–Shimomoto, Ideal-adic completion of quasi-excellent rings (after Gabber), Theorem 5.1, Step 1; obtained in sandbox sources/kurano40.pdf (bibliographic integration requested in report.md).

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-qe-minimal-formal-defect] to this $R,x$. Choose a triple $(L,\mathfrak n,\mathfrak s)$ attaining its least height $h\geq2$. Write $B=B_L$ and $C=C_{L,\mathfrak n}$. Thus $\mathfrak s$ is a minimal singular prime of $C$ and $\mathfrak s\cap B=0$. Every $B_{\mathfrak q}$ of height at most $h$ is excellent. By [lem-per-qe-semilocal-defect-height], for every finite $\gamma\subset\operatorname{Max}B$ containing $\mathfrak n$, the ring $D_\gamma$ and contracted prime $\mathfrak s_\gamma$ have the stated comparisons, $\operatorname{ht}\mathfrak s_\gamma=h>0$, and every member of $\Delta_\gamma(x)$ has height $h+1$ in $B$. Use exactly the normalized definition of $\Delta_\gamma(x)$ from these lemmas; its alternative description supplies a prime minimal over $\mathfrak s_\gamma+xD_\gamma$.

source.place: Kurano–Shimomoto, Ideal-adic completion of quasi-excellent rings (after Gabber), Theorem 5.1, Step 2 and Claim 5.4; obtained in sandbox sources/kurano40.pdf (bibliographic integration requested in report.md).

proof.text: For each prime $\mathfrak q\subset B$ of height at most $h$, apply [lem-per-qe-alteration-regular-neighbourhood] with $J=xB$: $B$ is a Noetherian domain, $B_{\mathfrak q}$ is excellent by Step 3, and $B/xB$ is quasi-excellent by the reduction. Obtain $b_{\mathfrak q}\notin\mathfrak q$, schemes $X_{\mathfrak q,i}$ regular above $V(x)$, and a proper surjective witness $V_{\mathfrak q}$ with an open cover mapping to them. Put $\Omega=\bigcup_{\operatorname{ht}\mathfrak q\leq h}D(b_{\mathfrak q})\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}B$. It is open and contains every prime of height at most $h$.

source.place: Kurano–Shimomoto, Ideal-adic completion of quasi-excellent rings (after Gabber), Theorem 5.1, Step 3, (5.12)–(5.13); obtained in sandbox sources/kurano40.pdf (bibliographic integration requested in report.md).

proof.text: We show $\Delta(x)\cap\Omega=\varnothing$. Suppose $Q$ lies in the intersection. By [lem-per-qe-semilocal-defect-height], choose $\gamma$ and $\widetilde Q\supset\mathfrak s_\gamma+xD_\gamma$ contracting to $Q$. Choose $\mathfrak q$ with $Q\in D(b_{\mathfrak q})$. Both $\mathfrak s_\gamma$ and $\widetilde Q$ then lie in $\operatorname{Spec}D_\gamma[1/b_{\mathfrak q}]$: the former contracts to zero, and the latter contracts to $Q$. Base change the witness $V_{\mathfrak q}$ and its cover along $\operatorname{Spec}D_\gamma[1/b_{\mathfrak q}]\to D(b_{\mathfrak q})$. The new witness $V'$ is surjective by [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change] and closed by the universal closedness in [def-weil-proper-morphism].

source.place: Kurano–Shimomoto, Ideal-adic completion of quasi-excellent rings (after Gabber), Theorem 5.1, Step 3, final diagram, printed pp.13–14; obtained in sandbox sources/kurano40.pdf (bibliographic integration requested in report.md).

proof.text: Lift $\mathfrak s_\gamma$ to a point $\xi_2$ of $V'$, using that surjectivity. Since $\mathfrak s_\gamma\subseteq\widetilde Q$, apply [lem-trf-closed-map-specializing] to the closed map $V'\to\operatorname{Spec}D_\gamma[1/b_{\mathfrak q}]$: a specialization $\xi_1$ of $\xi_2$ lies above $\widetilde Q$. Choose a member $V_i'$ of the pulled-back open cover containing $\xi_1$. It also contains its generalization $\xi_2$. Their images $\eta_1,\eta_2$ in $X_i'=X_{\mathfrak q,i}\times_B D_\gamma$ satisfy $\eta_2\rightsquigarrow\eta_1$. Write $\zeta_1$ for the image of $\eta_1$ in $X_{\mathfrak q,i}$. Its image in $\operatorname{Spec}B$ is $Q$, which contains $x$, so its local ring is regular by the closed-fibre conclusion of [lem-per-qe-alteration-regular-neighbourhood].

source.place: Kurano–Shimomoto, Ideal-adic completion of quasi-excellent rings (after Gabber), Theorem 5.1, Step 3, printed p.14, specialization lifting; obtained in sandbox sources/kurano40.pdf (bibliographic integration requested in report.md).

proof.text: The map $B\to D_\gamma$ is flat by [lem-per-qe-semilocal-defect-height]; hence [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map-iff-flat-affine] makes the affine scheme map flat, and the local map $\mathcal O_{X_{\mathfrak q,i},\zeta_1}\to\mathcal O_{X_i',\eta_1}$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change] and [def-weil-flat-morphism]. Its closed fibre is a field: $x\in Q$ and $D_\gamma/xD_\gamma\simeq B_\gamma/xB_\gamma$ identify $\operatorname{Spec}D_\gamma\times_B V(x)$ with the corresponding localization of $V(x)$, so base change over $\zeta_1$ has a single reduced point with residue field $\kappa(\zeta_1)$. The source is regular by Step 6. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-over-regular-with-regular-fibre] to obtain regularity at $\eta_1$. All these local rings are Noetherian: $D_\gamma$ is Noetherian and the charts $X_i'$ are of finite type over it.

source.place: Kurano–Shimomoto, Ideal-adic completion of quasi-excellent rings (after Gabber), Theorem 5.1, Step 3, printed p.14, flat closed-fibre comparison; obtained in sandbox sources/kurano40.pdf (bibliographic integration requested in report.md).

proof.text: Since $\eta_2$ generalizes $\eta_1$, [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-localization] gives regularity at $\eta_2$. The local map $(D_\gamma)_{\mathfrak s_\gamma}\to\mathcal O_{X_i',\eta_2}$ is flat: its point in $\operatorname{Spec}B$ is the generic point because $\mathfrak s_\gamma\cap B=0$. Thus it is a localization of a base change from a field; tensoring vector spaces is exact. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-under-regular] to this local map. It makes $(D_\gamma)_{\mathfrak s_\gamma}$ regular, contradicting [lem-per-qe-semilocal-defect-height]. This proves $\Delta(x)\subseteq\Omega^c$.

source.place: Kurano–Shimomoto, Ideal-adic completion of quasi-excellent rings (after Gabber), Theorem 5.1, Step 3, last paragraph, printed p.14; obtained in sandbox sources/kurano40.pdf (bibliographic integration requested in report.md).

proof.text: Write the closed set $\Omega^c$ as $V(H)$. By [lem-sc-finite-minimal-primes-over-ideal], $H$ has finitely many minimal primes. Every prime in $V(H)$ has height at least $h+1$, since $\Omega$ contains the primes of height at most $h$. A height-$(h+1)$ member $Q$ of $V(H)$ must itself be minimal over $H$: if $P\subsetneq Q$ were a minimal prime over $H$, a chain of length at least $h+1$ ending at $P$, followed by $P\subsetneq Q$, would force $\operatorname{ht}Q\geq h+2$. By [lem-per-qe-semilocal-defect-height], every member of $\Delta(x)$ has height $h+1$, so Step 8 puts $\Delta(x)$ inside this finite set of minimal primes. Hence $\Delta(x)$ is finite.

source.place: Kurano–Shimomoto, Ideal-adic completion of quasi-excellent rings (after Gabber), Theorem 5.1, Step 3, printed p.13, finiteness of the boundary; obtained in sandbox sources/kurano40.pdf (bibliographic integration requested in report.md).

proof.text: Finally apply [lem-per-qe-rotthaus-finite-boundary] with this $B,x,\mathfrak n,\mathfrak s$. The ring $B$ is Noetherian Nagata and $(x)$-adically complete by [lem-per-qe-normal-counterexample-reduction]; $\mathfrak s$ is a minimal singular prime of $C$ by [lem-per-qe-minimal-formal-defect]; the contracted primes have positive height $h$ by [lem-per-qe-semilocal-defect-height]; and Step 9 proves finiteness of the very same normalized $\Delta(x)$. The criterion gives $\mathfrak s\cap B\ne0$, contradicting the chosen triple. Thus $A$ is quasi-excellent. Together with Step 1 this proves both implications.

source.place: Kurano–Shimomoto, Ideal-adic completion of quasi-excellent rings (after Gabber), Theorem 5.1, Step 3, application of Theorem 5.3; obtained in sandbox sources/kurano40.pdf (bibliographic integration requested in report.md).
